:::{#thm-deriv-llik-iid}
#### Derivative of the log-likelihood function for $\iid$ data

For $\iid$ data:

$$\ell'(\theta) = \sumin \deriv{\theta} \log{\p(X = x_i \mid \theta)}$$ {#eq-deriv-llik}

:::

:::{.proof}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\lik'(\th)
&= \deriv{\th} \lik(\th)
&& \text{(notation for the derivative)}\\
&= \deriv{\th} \sum_{i=1}^n \log{\p(X = x_i \mid \theta)}
&& \text{(log-likelihood of an $\iid$ sample)}\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^n \deriv{\th} \log{\p(X = x_i \mid \theta)}
&& \text{(derivative of a sum is the sum of derivatives)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Unlike @eq-deriv-Lik, each term involves only one observation,
so no product rule is needed.
:::
